>

That doesn't mean that you can't `ln -s "$(command -v gsed)" "${AMDATADIR}"/bin/sed` instead of the hardcoded `ln -s /usr/local/bin/gsed  "${AMDATADIR}"/bin/sed`

`gsed` is somewhere on the system, there is no need to patch it at all in the script since all that has to be done is change `PATH` before running the install script that wants `sed`, and since the symlink will be named `sed` and points to `gsed` that's all that needs to be done.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
"AppMan" has been successfully installed!

Proposed output
```
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
"AppMan" has been successfully installed!

To use 'appman' in your current terminal, please run

Then, run "appman -h" to see the list of the options.

Agree with @ivan-hc - auto-confirming a guessed name is risky regardless of `-y`. This flow exists to catch a typo, not to pick a package for the user.

For both the single-guess prompt and the new candidate list, I'd apply the same rule as the sandbox prompts: when `-y` is set, don't prompt and don't auto-pick a guess - just show the normal "does NOT exist" error and stop there.

Agreed. We still need a method to abort instead of prompt, though.

@ivan-hc how about we rename the variables to be **yn_abort**/**choice_abort**:
```
_read $" Select a number (0 to cancel): " choice_abort
...
...
_read $" Install \"$DID_YOU_MEAN\" with --$DID_YOU_MEAN_FLAG flag? (Y/n) " yn_abort
```

Then in _read:
```
elif [[ "$var_name" == "choice_abort" ]]; then
	results="0"
elif [[ "$var_name" == "yn_abort" ]]; then
	results="n"
```

Selecting 'N' or '0' will abort the operation, will work for the sandbox parts as well and will make `-y` fully non-interactive. So for dangerous operations, we just rename them to **yn_abort** or **choice_abort**.

I believe APT also behaves this way, it will not allow -y for dangerous operations and will just directly abort.

body:
Works great!

But the `Exec` line here is one giant line with the whole script crammed into it. It's really hard to read and edit.

 Suggestion: pull the script out into its own file (e.g. `$DATADIR/AM-pla-install-handler.sh`, written the same way with a heredoc), and make `Exec` just point to it:
